verses.text:
In the 1611 King James Version, Genesis 1:6 marks the first instance where “the King’s Printer” Robert Barker uses a pilcrow (¶) to mark the beginning of a new paragraph. Here, Acts 20:36 marks the last time where a pilcrow is used.
One may assume it to be due to logistical or theological reasons, but the fact is that there are no records of why Robert Barker and his crew stopped using the pilcrow after Acts 20:36. I can only point out that Robert Barker and his colleague Martin Lucas would later be fined for their sloppy craftsmanship in the 1631 KJV, which gives reason to attribute the pilcrow’s disappearance to poor logistics. (See Exodus 20:14 for more.)
